test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 30 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The value of a machine depreciates at the rate of 10% per annum. If its present value is Rs. 1,62,000, then what will be its worth after 2 years?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Depreciation rate = 10% = 1/10 → Value becomes 9/10 each year.

Worth after 2 years = Present Value × (9/10)²

Worth = 1,62,000 × (81/100) = 1,620 × 81

Worth = 1,31,220

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,31,220.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Present Value (P) = Rs. 1,62,000, Rate of depreciation (R) = 10% per annum, Time (n) = 2 years.

**Formula Used:** Worth after n years = P × (1 − R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cf75cf5842a73486a8ba1b0e6e14aee8a44f5a5cc0ffc6baa8667adad075b51a.png] 

⇒ Worth = 1,62,000 × (1 − 10/100)²

⇒ Worth = 1,62,000 × (90/100) × (90/100)

⇒ Worth = 1,62,000 × 0.9 × 0.9

⇒ Worth = 1,62,000 × 0.81

⇒ Worth = 1,31,220

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,31,220.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Depreciation Formula

When the value of an object decreases at a constant rate, the final value is A = P(1 − R/100)ⁿ.

Successive Percentage Change

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the effective change is [a + b + (ab/100)]%. For 10% depreciation, a = −10 and b = −10, giving −19% total change.

Appreciation

If the value increases (like population or land price), the formula becomes A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ.</p
